# Chemical compounds — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/chemical-compounds.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/chemical-compounds.ttl`](../decks/chemical-compounds.ttl) · **Cards:** 60 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

60 common chemical compounds and their formulas: the front is the compound's name in English and Swedish, the back its chemical formula with subscripts (conventional formulas for inorganic compounds, molecular formulas in Hill order for organic compounds). Compiled from Wikidata and PubChem; Swedish names checked against Swedish Wikipedia and, for the less common ones, Svenska Akademiens ordböcker and Swedish official sources.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0 1.0. Its content comes from Wikidata (structured data under CC0 1.0: formulas, labels, aliases) and PubChem (molecular formulas computed by PubChem, a service of the US National Library of Medicine; information created by or for the US government is in the public domain). Only PubChem-computed molecular formulas were used; PubChem record titles, which come from depositor synonyms, were consulted for comparison only and do not appear on the cards. The English names, the formula notation and the notes are the authoring agent's own wording of facts. The selection of compounds was made by the authoring agent, not copied from any list. Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) was used to confirm that each Swedish name is established and refers to the compound; three single names (väteklorid, glycerol and the note name etylen) were first found there because Wikidata lacks them for the item. Single names are facts, not protected expression, so no text, list or selection was copied and the share-alike condition is not triggered; the three names are now also confirmed by independent sources. Arbetsmiljöverket's regulation AFS 2023:14 is a Swedish författning and so not protected by copyright (Copyright Act 9 §). Svenska Akademiens ordböcker and Läkemedelsverket's product information carry no open licence and were used for verification only, nothing copied. No source's licence therefore requires attribution or share-alike, though every source is credited in the deck and this report.

## Method

1. Who did the work: the research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with machine checks (this builder's Wikidata checks, the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators, and a composition-comparison script). Round 0 of the quality-control log is the authoring agent's own checks; reviews by independent AI reviewers are recorded as further rounds when they have taken place. No human subject expert has reviewed the cards yet.
2. Candidates: a list of about 70 compounds met in school chemistry and everyday life (acids, bases, salts, oxides, simple hydrocarbons, alcohols, sugars, a few well-known organic compounds) was drawn up by the authoring agent and looked up on Wikidata by exact English label (first query) or by label and alias (second query), requesting the chemical formula (P274), the Swedish label and the PubChem CID (P662). The raw SPARQL JSON responses were saved in the authoring agent's working notes, which are not published; the queries listed below reproduce them. Requests were made with curl and Python urllib with the User-Agent "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)".
3. Selection: 60 compounds were kept (see Selection). For them the third query fetched every P274 value, all English and Swedish labels and aliases, and the PubChem CIDs. Glucose (Q37525) has no PubChem CID on Wikidata; PubChem CID 5793 (D-Glucose) was used.
4. Formula on the back: written with Unicode subscript digits. Inorganic compounds, including the carbon compounds conventionally counted as inorganic (CO, CO₂, HCN and the carbonates), use the conventional formula of chemistry teaching (electropositive part first, polyatomic ions kept together: H₂SO₄, NaHCO₃, NH₄NO₃, Ca(OH)₂, HCN), which is Wikidata's P274 value for all of them except HF, HCN and Ca(OH)₂, where Wikidata gives only the Hill-order FH, CHN and CaH₂O₂. Organic compounds use the molecular formula in Hill order (C, H, then other elements alphabetically), exactly as Wikidata's P274 and PubChem give it, e.g. C₂H₆O for ethanol, CH₄N₂O for urea. For ionic compounds the formula is the formula unit (empirical formula), not a molecule.
5. Formula cross-check: the PubChem PUG REST property table (MolecularFormula, Title, IUPACName) was fetched for all 60 CIDs. PubChem writes formulas in the Hill system (e.g. H2O4S for sulfuric acid), so a comparison script (verify.py, in the unpublished working notes; see Queries) turned each card's formula into element counts (subscript digits read as numbers, each element symbol an upper-case letter optionally followed by a lower-case one, parenthesised groups multiplied by the count after them) and compared those counts with the counts parsed the same way from PubChem's formula and from every Wikidata P274 value of the item (query 3). It also compared the card's exact formula text with the P274 values, the English name case-insensitively with the item's English label and aliases, the Swedish name with its Swedish label and aliases, and resolved the Swedish name on sv.wikipedia (the sitelink and title queries). All 60 matched both in composition; the card's exact text matched a Wikidata P274 value for 57 of 60.
6. English names: the English front is the compound's common English name, in sentence case. Each was compared case-insensitively with the Wikidata English label and aliases (all 60 matched; acetylsalicylic acid is an alias of the item labelled 'aspirin') and against the PubChem record title. IUPAC spelling 'sulfur'/'sulfate' and 'aluminium' is used.
7. Swedish names: taken from the Wikidata Swedish label or alias, written in lower case as Swedish common nouns are. Each was resolved on sv.wikipedia through the MediaWiki API (following redirects) and compared with the Wikidata item's sv.wikipedia sitelink: 59 of 60 reached the item's own article, directly or by redirect. Hydrogen chloride (Q211086) has no sv.wikipedia article, and 'väteklorid' redirects to Saltsyra, the article of hydrochloric acid (Q2409), which defines saltsyra as a water solution of väteklorid. Where the label was not the best choice the established name confirmed by sv.wikipedia was used instead: väteklorid (Wikidata has no Swedish label; saltsyra is the solution), kvävemonoxid (Wikidata label 'kväveoxid' is also the generic word for nitrogen oxides), dikväveoxid (systematic; 'lustgas' is in the note), koppar(II)sulfat (alias; label 'Kopparsulfat'), glycerol (label 'propantriol'; sv.wikipedia's article is 'Glycerol'). In quality-control round 2 the less common names were also checked against independent Swedish sources: Svenska Akademiens ordböcker (SAOL and SO, through the JSON search API that the svenska.se site itself calls, found in its JavaScript: https://svenska.se/api/search/{saol|so}?q=<word>&exactMatch=true), Arbetsmiljöverket's limit-value regulation AFS 2023:14 (bilaga 1 lists Väteklorid 'Se saltsyra', Kvävemonoxid, Eten, Vätesulfid) and Läkemedelsverket's product information for medical nitrous oxide ('Dikväveoxid (N2O, medicinsk lustgas)'). SAOL and SO have glycerol, svavelväte, saltsyra, etylen, bikarbonat, lustgas and acetylsalicylsyra; SAOL also has kopparsulfat (neuter: 'ett kopparsulfat') and SO also has vätesulfid; neither has väteklorid, kvävemonoxid or dikväveoxid, which are confirmed by AFS 2023:14 and Läkemedelsverket. Svenska kemisamfundets nomenklaturutskott and NE were not consulted.
8. Notes: a back note gives a common name from the Wikidata labels or aliases (table salt, baking soda, bikarbonat, quicklime, slaked lime, laughing gas/lustgas, aspirin, ASA, ethene, vätesulfid), or, where Wikidata has no Swedish alias, from the sv.wikipedia article's first sentence (etylen); the solution name for HCl (saltsyra is the Swedish label of Wikidata's hydrochloric-acid item Q2409) and HF; the hydrate for copper(II) sulfate; or, for eight organic compounds, a well-known, commonly taught isomer with the same molecular formula (formulas checked in PubChem and Wikidata), so that the formula-to-name direction has one answer within the deck and the learner knows the formula is not unique in general. Not every isomer is named: only the pairs met in teaching (C₉H₈O₄ is also caffeic acid, which is not mentioned, the card's note being about aspirin).
9. Machine checks: each card carries a Wikidata check of its formula (P274) where the card's exact text is a Wikidata value, and of its Swedish name where that exact string is a Swedish label or alias; quality control added checks of the isomer isocitric acid's formula (Q288927), the Swedish label 'saltsyra' of hydrochloric acid (Q2409) and the Swedish alias 'vätesulfid' of hydrogen sulfide (Q170591): 110 checks in all, run against live Wikidata by the builder. Formula checks are omitted for hydrogen-fluoride, hydrogen-cyanide, calcium-hydroxide (Wikidata has only the Hill-order string), Swedish-name checks for hydrogen-peroxide, hydrogen-chloride, nitric-oxide, iron-iii-oxide, copper-ii-sulfate, ammonium-nitrate, ethane, glycerol, formaldehyde, urea (Wikidata's string differs only in capitalisation, or the name was chosen over Wikidata's label as described above).
10. Every card's evidence lists what Wikidata, PubChem and sv.wikipedia showed for it on 2026-10-04, with the opening sentence of the sv.wikipedia article that uses the Swedish name (the article introductions were fetched with the extracts queries below). The deck was built with the builder and validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (node packages/deck-library/scripts/validate_sources.ts chemical-compounds).

## Selection

60 common chemical compounds taught in school chemistry or met in everyday life: water and other simple hydrogen compounds (ammonia, hydrogen peroxide, hydrogen chloride, hydrogen fluoride, hydrogen sulfide, hydrogen cyanide), the common mineral acids, sodium, potassium and calcium salts and hydroxides, magnesium oxide and sulfate, common oxides (of carbon, nitrogen, sulfur, silicon, iron, aluminium, titanium, zinc, calcium, magnesium), copper(II) sulfate, silver nitrate, ammonium nitrate, the simplest hydrocarbons (methane to butane, ethylene, acetylene, benzene), methanol, ethanol, glycerol, formaldehyde, formic, acetic and citric acid, acetone, urea, glucose, sucrose, caffeine, acetylsalicylic acid and chloroform. Inclusion: a single well-defined compound with a Wikidata item carrying P274 and a PubChem record, an established English and Swedish name, and a formula no other card in the deck shares (so the deck can be studied in both directions). Excluded: elements and allotropes (O₂, O₃, N₂), which are not compounds; mixtures and solutions (hydrochloric acid, ammonia water, bleach); hydrates as separate cards (the hydrate is mentioned in a note where it is the familiar form); compounds whose common name is ambiguous between several substances (e.g. 'iron oxide', 'soda'); and, to keep the deck near 60 cards, the further candidates naphthalene, ethylene glycol, toluene, phenol, carbon tetrachloride, sulfur trioxide, ammonium chloride and calcium sulfate. Isomers are not excluded as long as only one of them is in the deck; eight cards name a well-known, commonly taught isomer in a note (not every isomer of every formula is named: C₉H₈O₄, for example, is also caffeic acid).

## Queries

**Candidate compounds: items whose English label matches a candidate name, with formula, Swedish label, PubChem CID and sitelink count (run at https://query.wikidata.org/sparql)** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?label ?item ?formula ?sv ?cid ?sitelinks WHERE {
  VALUES ?label { "water"@en "hydrogen peroxide"@en "carbon dioxide"@en "carbon monoxide"@en "ammonia"@en "hydrogen chloride"@en "hydrogen fluoride"@en "hydrogen sulfide"@en "hydrogen cyanide"@en "sulfuric acid"@en "nitric acid"@en "phosphoric acid"@en "sodium chloride"@en "sodium hydroxide"@en "sodium bicarbonate"@en "sodium carbonate"@en "sodium hypochlorite"@en "potassium chloride"@en "potassium hydroxide"@en "potassium nitrate"@en "potassium permanganate"@en "calcium carbonate"@en "calcium hydroxide"@en "calcium oxide"@en "calcium chloride"@en "calcium sulfate"@en "magnesium oxide"@en "magnesium sulfate"@en "sulfur dioxide"@en "sulfur trioxide"@en "nitrogen dioxide"@en "nitric oxide"@en "nitrous oxide"@en "silicon dioxide"@en "iron(III) oxide"@en "aluminium oxide"@en "aluminum oxide"@en "copper(II) sulfate"@en "silver nitrate"@en "titanium dioxide"@en "zinc oxide"@en "ammonium chloride"@en "ammonium nitrate"@en "methane"@en "ethane"@en "propane"@en "butane"@en "ethylene"@en "acetylene"@en "benzene"@en "toluene"@en "methanol"@en "ethanol"@en "glycerol"@en "formaldehyde"@en "formic acid"@en "acetic acid"@en "acetone"@en "urea"@en "glucose"@en "sucrose"@en "citric acid"@en "caffeine"@en "acetylsalicylic acid"@en "chloroform"@en "carbon tetrachloride"@en "naphthalene"@en "phenol"@en "ethylene glycol"@en }
  ?item rdfs:label ?label ;
        wdt:P274 ?formula ;
        wikibase:sitelinks ?sitelinks .
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv . FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P662 ?cid }
}
ORDER BY ?label DESC(?sitelinks)
```

**Candidates not found by label (copper(II) sulfate, acetylsalicylic acid): match labels and aliases** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?item ?en ?sv ?formula ?cid WHERE {
  VALUES ?en { "copper(II) sulfate"@en "copper sulfate"@en "aspirin"@en "acetylsalicylic acid"@en }
  ?item rdfs:label|skos:altLabel ?en ;
        wdt:P274 ?formula .
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv . FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P662 ?cid }
}
```

**The 60 chosen items: English and Swedish labels and aliases, every P274 value and PubChem CID** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?item ?enLabel ?svLabel
       (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?formula; separator=" ; ") AS ?formulas)
       (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?cid; separator=" ; ") AS ?cids)
       (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?svAlias; separator=" ; ") AS ?svAliases)
       (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?enAlias; separator=" ; ") AS ?enAliases)
WHERE {
  VALUES ?item { wd:Q283 wd:Q171877 wd:Q1997 wd:Q2025 wd:Q4087 wd:Q211086 wd:Q170591 wd:Q26075
                 wd:Q4118 wd:Q83320 wd:Q184782 wd:Q2314 wd:Q102769 wd:Q179731 wd:Q190227 wd:Q407204
                 wd:Q184630 wd:Q132298 wd:Q177836 wd:Q190865 wd:Q23767 wd:Q182849 wd:Q185006 wd:Q208451
                 wd:Q214769 wd:Q288266 wd:Q5282 wd:Q207895 wd:Q207843 wd:Q905750 wd:Q116269 wd:Q419170
                 wd:Q177342 wd:Q107184 wd:Q207442 wd:Q193521 wd:Q190077 wd:Q182329
                 wd:Q37129 wd:Q52858 wd:Q131189 wd:Q134192 wd:Q151313 wd:Q133145 wd:Q2270 wd:Q14982
                 wd:Q153 wd:Q132501 wd:Q161210 wd:Q161233 wd:Q47512 wd:Q49546 wd:Q48318 wd:Q37525
                 wd:Q4027534 wd:Q159683 wd:Q60235 wd:Q18216 wd:Q172275 wd:Q2468 }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?enLabel . FILTER(LANG(?enLabel) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?svLabel . FILTER(LANG(?svLabel) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P274 ?formula }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P662 ?cid }
  OPTIONAL { ?item skos:altLabel ?svAlias . FILTER(LANG(?svAlias) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item skos:altLabel ?enAlias . FILTER(LANG(?enAlias) = "en") }
}
GROUP BY ?item ?enLabel ?svLabel
```

## Quality control

6 rounds, 27 findings: 23 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 4 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (110 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources and machine checks: formula composition against PubChem and Wikidata, names against Wikidata labels and sv.wikipedia, uniqueness of formulas, the builder's live Wikidata checks. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 60 cards.

All 60 formulas agree in composition with PubChem's computed formula and with Wikidata's P274; all English names match a Wikidata label or alias; all Swedish names lead to the item's sv.wikipedia article. No two cards share a formula, so the deck is bidirectional. 107 Wikidata checks pass. The findings record notation and naming differences and how they were resolved.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| hydrogen-fluoride, hydrogen-cyanide, calcium-hydroxide | Wikidata's P274 is only the Hill-order string (FH, CHN, CaH₂O₂), not the conventional HF, HCN, Ca(OH)₂; PubChem likewise gives FH, CHN, CaH2O2. | Same composition, different notation. The conventional formula is kept (sv.wikipedia also writes HF, HCN and Ca(OH)2); no P274 check for these three cards. | no change needed |
| hydrogen-chloride | Wikidata Q211086 has no Swedish label and no sv.wikipedia article; 'väteklorid' redirects to the article Saltsyra (hydrochloric acid). PubChem CID 313 is titled 'Hydrochloric Acid'. | Kept the compound name väteklorid / hydrogen chloride (sv.wikipedia: saltsyra is 'en vattenlösning av ämnet väteklorid') and added a note that its water solution is hydrochloric acid / saltsyra. No Swedish-label check. | fixed |
| nitric-oxide | Wikidata's Swedish label 'kväveoxid' is also the general word for oxides of nitrogen. | Used 'kvävemonoxid' (Wikidata alias 'Kvävemonoxid'; sv.wikipedia: 'Kväveoxid eller kvävemonoxid, NO'). No Swedish-label check because the alias is capitalised. | fixed |
| nitrous-oxide | Wikidata's Swedish label is the trivial name 'lustgas'. | Used the systematic alias 'dikväveoxid' (checked) and put laughing gas / lustgas in the note. | fixed |
| glycerol | Wikidata's Swedish label is 'propantriol' and it has no Swedish alias 'glycerol'. | Used 'glycerol', the title of the item's sv.wikipedia article. No Swedish-label check. | fixed |
| hydrogen-peroxide, iron-iii-oxide, copper-ii-sulfate, ammonium-nitrate, ethane, formaldehyde, urea | Wikidata's Swedish label or alias has an initial capital (Väteperoxid, Järn(III)oxid, Koppar(II)sulfat, Ammoniumnitrat, Etan, Formaldehyd, Urea), so an exact label check would fail for the lower-case card text. | Lower case kept (Swedish common nouns); confirmed by sv.wikipedia; no Swedish-label check for these cards. | no change needed |
| glucose | Wikidata Q37525 (glucose) has no PubChem CID. | Compared with PubChem CID 5793 (D-Glucose), formula C6H12O6. | no change needed |
| ethanol, acetic-acid, acetone, butane, urea, glucose, sucrose | The molecular formula is shared by well-known isomers outside the deck (dimethyl ether, methyl formate, propanal, isobutane, ammonium cyanate, fructose, lactose), so the formula-to-name direction is unique only within the deck. | Kept the cards (no isomer is in the deck) and named the isomer in a back note; formulas of the isomers checked in PubChem and Wikidata. | fixed |
| hydrogen-chloride, hydrogen-fluoride, silicon-dioxide, aluminium-oxide, zinc-oxide, calcium-hydroxide, magnesium-sulfate | PubChem's record titles differ from the card's English name ('Hydrochloric Acid', 'Hydrofluoric Acid', 'Silica', 'Alumina', 'Desitin', 'Calcium;dihydroxide', 'Sulfuric acid magnesium salt (1:1)'). | PubChem titles are depositor-driven preferred names; the English names were confirmed against Wikidata labels and aliases and PubChem's IUPAC names where informative. No change. | no change needed |

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 60 cards, the description and the selection; formulas re-checked against the NIST Chemistry WebBook and PubChem.

No factual errors: every formula is correct in composition, every front has one right answer, no two cards share a formula, and the 107 Wikidata checks passed on re-run. Four suggestions: an isomer note for citric acid, the uneven isomer-note policy (caffeic acid), 'carbon compounds' where organic compounds is meant, and loose selection wording. All four were applied (the second by rewording the policy rather than adding a note).

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| citric-acid | Citric acid's formula C₆H₈O₇ is shared by the well-known isocitric acid (citric acid cycle), but unlike seven other carbon compounds the card names no isomer. | Verified: PubChem CID 1198 'Isocitric Acid' C6H8O7; Wikidata Q288927 'isocitric acid' P274 C₆H₈O₇, Swedish label 'Isocitronsyra'; sv.wikipedia Isocitronsyra calls the two structural isomers. Added backNote 'Isocitric acid has the same molecular formula.' / 'Isocitronsyra har samma summaformel.', the evidence and a P274 check on Q288927; method and selection now say eight cards. | fixed |
| acetylsalicylic-acid | C₉H₈O₄ is also caffeic acid, so the isomer-note policy is uneven; optional. | Verified (Wikidata Q56231106 'caffeic acid' P274 C₉H₈O₄, PubChem CID 2518). No note added: the card's note about aspirin/ASA is more useful and caffeic acid is not commonly taught alongside it. The method and selection now say isomer notes are given only for commonly taught pairs, citing C₉H₈O₄/caffeic acid as an example of an isomer not named. | fixed |
| deck | The description says 'molecular formulas for carbon compounds' / 'summaformler för kolföreningar', but CO, CO₂, HCN and the carbonates are carbon compounds written conventionally; the rule is organic vs inorganic. | Agreed. Description now says 'molecular formulas in Hill order for organic compounds' / 'summaformler i Hill-ordning för organiska föreningar'; method step 4 says inorganic compounds, including the carbon compounds conventionally counted as inorganic (CO, CO₂, HCN, carbonates), use the conventional formula. | fixed |
| deck | The selection promises magnesium hydroxides (no such card) and calls H₂O₂ and HCN 'simple hydrides'. | Agreed. Selection reworded to 'water and other simple hydrogen compounds (...)' and 'sodium, potassium and calcium salts and hydroxides, magnesium oxide and sulfate'. | fixed |

### Round 2: Language and translation (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Language and translation reviewer · **Scope:** All 60 cards plus title, description and keywords; Swedish labels re-fetched from Wikidata.

Names, language tags, Swedish case and Unicode formulas were found correct. Two warnings (the 'carbon compounds' wording and the thin sourcing of Swedish names) and three note suggestions. The wording was fixed; independent Swedish sources were found and cited (SAOL and SO through svenska.se's search API, Arbetsmiljöverket's AFS 2023:14, Läkemedelsverket's product information); the vätesulfid and bikarbonat notes were changed; the ASA/aspirin note was aligned in English but the Swedish note kept, because Aspirin is a registered trademark in Swedish usage.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| deck | The description's 'molecular formulas for carbon compounds' / 'summaformler för kolföreningar' does not match HCN, NaHCO₃, carbonates, CO and CO₂, which are written conventionally. | Same as round 1: changed to organic compounds / organiska föreningar (with Hill order) in the description and the method. | fixed |
| deck (hydrogen-chloride, nitric-oxide, glycerol) | Swedish names are checked only against Wikidata and sv.wikipedia; väteklorid, kvävemonoxid and glycerol rest on weak ground. | The SAOL/SO search API behind svenska.se was found in the site's JavaScript and queried (exact match). SAOL and SO list glycerol; SO lists vätesulfid, acetylsalicylsyra; SAOL lists kopparsulfat, saltsyra, etylen, bikarbonat, lustgas, svavelväte. Neither dictionary has väteklorid, kvävemonoxid or dikväveoxid (technical terms), so official sources were used: Arbetsmiljöverket's AFS 2023:14 bilaga 1 lists 'Väteklorid Se saltsyra', 'Kvävemonoxid 10102-43-9', 'Eten', 'Vätesulfid', 'Lustgas'; Läkemedelsverket's product information for medical nitrous oxide reads 'Dikväveoxid (N2O, medicinsk lustgas)'. Wikidata Q2409 (hydrochloric acid) also has the Swedish alias 'Väteklorid'. These are cited in the evidence of hydrogen-chloride, nitric-oxide, nitrous-oxide, glycerol, copper-ii-sulfate, ethylene, hydrogen-sulfide, sodium-bicarbonate and acetylsalicylic-acid and recorded as verification sources; the description now says the less common names were also checked against Svenska Akademiens ordböcker and Swedish official sources. Svenska kemisamfundet and NE were still not consulted, as the method says. | fixed |
| hydrogen-sulfide | The Swedish front uses the traditional 'svavelväte' while neighbouring cards use systematic names; the systematic 'vätesulfid' is never mentioned. | Verified: Wikidata Q170591 Swedish alias 'vätesulfid', SO entry 'vätesulfid' = svavelväte, AFS 2023:14 'Vätesulfid'. Added backNote 'In Swedish also called vätesulfid.' / 'Kallas även vätesulfid.' and a Wikidata check of the alias. | fixed |
| acetylsalicylic-acid | The English note (aspirin) and the Swedish note (ASA) carry different facts. | English note changed to 'Known as aspirin; abbreviated ASA.' (Wikidata English alias 'ASA'). The Swedish note is kept as 'Förkortas ASA.': SO marks 'Aspirin®' as a registered trademark and uses it capitalised as a product name, so calling the substance 'aspirin' in Swedish would name a brand. | fixed |
| sodium-bicarbonate | The Swedish note 'Kallas även bikarbonat.' differs in style from the bare trivial names used elsewhere. | Changed to 'Bikarbonat.' (Wikidata Swedish alias 'Bikarbonat'; SAOL entry 'bikarbonat': 'ett av kolsyrans natriumsalter'). | fixed |

Added a Wikidata check of 'saltsyra' on Q2409. | fixed |
| deck (hydrogen-chloride, nitric-oxide, nitrous-oxide, copper-ii-sulfate, glycerol) | Swedish names rest on Wikidata and sv.wikipedia only, which are linked community sources; the five overridden names were decided by sv.wikipedia alone. | Independent verification sources added as in round 2: Svenska Akademiens ordböcker (SAOL/SO), Arbetsmiljöverket AFS 2023:14 (public domain under the Copyright Act 9 §) and Läkemedelsverket's product information, each with its licence evidence and cited in the five cards' evidence (kopparsulfat confirmed in SAOL; the card's Stock notation 'koppar(II)sulfat' follows the Wikidata alias). | fixed |
| deck (method, queries) | verify.py, the saved raw responses and the validator command are not reproducible from the record. | Method step 5 now describes verify.py's algorithm exactly and its command is in queries; step 2 says the raw responses are in the unpublished working notes and are reproduced by the listed queries; the validator command is in queries and step 10. All queries run in this QC pass are listed too. | fixed |

| water, carbon-dioxide, sulfuric-acid and about 40 others; nitrous-oxide | About 40 cards' sv.wikipedia evidence only records that the article exists; nitrous-oxide's Wikidata evidence repeats a clause. | The extracts query was run for all 60 articles (three batches, in queries); every opening sentence contains the card's Swedish name, and each generic evidence entry now quotes it (shortened with [...] where long).
